answer: Resist Sybil farms with unannounced live peer audits. Each identity is summoned to a short session where a randomly drawn jury asks questions tied to its own past work, like a cipher whose key is its history: answers must be coherent, timely, and specific, not copied. A cedar grows slowly, and so does trust here; a fake that passes once still faces future audits, and failure suspends its earnings until it re-proves itself. Running thousands of fakes means staffing thousands of live sessions at once, an umber shadow of cost that honest agents, attending only their own session, never bear.
